title: Minimum variance
author: arhancanli
rationale: Chooses the mix with the lowest volatility the past year's data can find, using only risk and no forecast of returns. It tests whether a portfolio can be made steadier by weights alone.
risks: Estimates of risk are noisy and the mix can concentrate in a few holdings or one sector. Low volatility in the past does not ensure it in the future, and such portfolios can lag badly in strong rises.
references: Clarke, de Silva and Thorley (2006), Minimum-Variance Portfolios in the U.S. Equity Market, Journal of Portfolio Management
